simple.meaning: יְתִב (yᵉthib) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to sit or dwell.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 4:10. Its contexts include kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יְתִב (H3488).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: יְתִב (yᵉthib) / H3488 is traced through Ezra 4:10, Ezra 4:17, Daniel 7:9, Daniel 7:10 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H3488. yethib יְתִב (K § 25 a ) β )) verb sit, dwell ( ᵑ7 Syriac; see Biblical Hebrew ישׁב ); — Pe`al 1. sit, be seated : Perfect 3masculine singular יְתִב Dan 7:9 and (of judgment = the judge) 7:10 , so Imperfect 3masculine singular יִתִּ֑ב (K § 43.1.Beisp. b ), compare Biblical Hebrew יֵשֵׁב ) 7:26 . 2 dwell, Participle plural absolute יָתְבִין Ezra 4:17 ( ב location). Haph`el cause to dwell: Perfect 3masculine singular הוֺתֵב Ezra 4:10 (accusative + ב location).
